descriptors.evidence: numeric_parseable_fraction 0.9996 and short mean_value_length (2.95) match a compact numeric spec, and its profile (fractional decimal samples '.02'-'.25', distinct=6071, uniqueness 0.1063) closely parallels dim_a/dim_b/dim_c. Highest occurrence count (57110) of any field suggests a near-universal numeric attribute (e.g. weight or a 4th physical measurement), but the generic anonymized name gives no way to confirm which spec it is.

numeric_parseable_fraction 0.9993, 2734 distinct values, low uniqueness (0.0586, many products share the same round dimension values) and short decimal samples ('.5','.66','0','0.1') are consistent with a physical product dimension (e.g. length/width/height in inches). Paired naming with dim_b/dim_c strongly implies one axis of a 3D dimension set, though which axis is not determinable from the data alone.

numeric_parseable_fraction 0.9999, 2604 distinct, uniqueness 0.0701, samples '0','0.04','0.08' - same shape as dim_a/dim_c, indicating this is a second physical dimension axis (furniture length/width/height family) rather than an independent concept.

numeric_parseable_fraction is a perfect 1.0 (unlike dim_a/dim_b which have a residual non-numeric sliver), 2006 distinct, uniqueness 0.0676, samples are clean fractional inches ('.2','.375','.5','.625','.75' - common woodworking fraction steps). Fits as the third axis of a product-dimension triple with dim_a/dim_b.

Name plus near-total numeric_parseable_fraction (0.9997) and low uniqueness (0.0351, many items share standard capacity values like '0.2','0.5') is exactly the shape expected of a weight-capacity spec for furniture (chairs, shelves, beds), a common real search/filter dimension in this vertical.

numeric_parseable_fraction 0.9991 with only 83 distinct values across 8602 occurrences and very low uniqueness (0.0096) and short mean length (2.03) suggests a small bucketed integer (count, percentage, or index) rather than a continuous measurement, but the generic name gives no reliable clue to its real-world meaning, so I treat it as an internal/ranking numeric signal rather than a confident shopper-facing filter.

Exactly 2 distinct values ('no','yes'), numeric_parseable_fraction 0.0, uniqueness 0.0001 - unambiguously a strict boolean flag. The anonymized name gives no clue which real commerce attribute (e.g. assembly-required, eco-friendly) it encodes, so identity confidence is low even though the boolean structure is certain.

2 distinct values ('no','yes'), numeric_parseable_fraction 0.0, uniqueness 0.0001, occurrence 25258 - a distinct boolean flag from flag_12 (different occurrence count implies a different underlying attribute), but real-world identity is unrecoverable from the anonymized name.

3 distinct values ('', 'no', 'yes') - a nullable/tri-state boolean (unknown/not-applicable plus yes/no), numeric_parseable_fraction 0.0. Same reasoning as other flag_* fields: structure is clearly boolean-with-missing, but specific commerce meaning is unrecoverable from the name alone.

3 distinct values ('', 'no', 'yes'), numeric_parseable_fraction 0.0, occurrence 7541 - a nullable boolean flag distinct from flag_14 by occurrence count; meaning cannot be pinned down from the generic name.

2 distinct values ('no','yes'), numeric_parseable_fraction 0.0, uniqueness 0.0002 - strict boolean, no empty/missing state recorded (unlike flag_14/15/18), suggesting this flag is populated whenever applicable.

2 distinct values ('no','yes'), numeric_parseable_fraction 0.0, occurrence 10779 - strict boolean flag, distinguishable from flag_16 only by occurrence count; underlying real attribute is unknown given the generic name.
3 distinct values ('', 'no', 'yes'), numeric_parseable_fraction 0.0 - nullable boolean flag, occurrence 12555. Same caveat as other flag_* fields on unknown real semantic identity.

70 distinct values, long mean length (15.2) of multi-word descriptors ('american traditional','asian inspired','apothecary'), very low uniqueness (0.0036, heavily shared across products) - a granular decor style/theme tag, exactly the kind of facet furniture shoppers query on directly ('asian inspired decor').

Only 16 distinct values vs tag_group_a's 70, shorter mean length (8.21), samples ('boho','coastal','country','country / farmhouse') read as a coarser top-level style taxonomy compared to tag_group_a's more granular theme tags - both are style facets but at different granularity.

71 distinct values that are literal country names ('afghanistan','argentina','australia','bahrain','bangladesh'), high occurrence (34034) - unambiguously a country-of-origin field. 'Made in USA' style filtering is a common furniture shopper query even though 'usa' isn't in the shown alphabetically-first samples.

Despite the name implying a boolean, distinct=10 and samples ('full','full assembly','full assembly needed','light') are clearly multi-valued phrases describing assembly level, not yes/no - this is a case where the field's real data overrides its misleading 'flag' name. 'No/some assembly required' is one of the most-used furniture search filters.

9 distinct values, all wood-tone/finish phrases ('dark brown wood','espresso wood','gray wood','light wood'). Notably includes 'esptresso wood', a typo-duplicate of 'espresso wood', showing the enum vocabulary is fragmented by data-entry errors that would need normalization before a clean bitmap facet works.

250 distinct values formatted as '<percentage> % <material>' ('100 % cotton','100 % fine porcelain','100 % medium density fiberboard','100 % water hyacinth'), spanning textiles and hard materials across very different product types - a primary-material composition field. The percentage prefix is noise relative to the material name shoppers actually search on.

77 distinct plain material names without percentage prefixes ('acacia wood','acrylic','aluminium','aluminum') - a cleaner/simpler material field than material_code. Note both British ('aluminium') and American ('aluminum') spellings appear as separate distinct values, direct evidence of enum fragmentation from spelling variants.

99 distinct values including 'amphora' and 'arabesque' (classic decor shape/silhouette vocabulary) alongside 'abstract/novelty' - reads as a decorative shape/form attribute for home-decor items (vases, mirrors, wall art) rather than a generic 'form' in the sense of physical dimension.

93 distinct values reading as art/pattern style descriptors ('abstract cubism','abstract/geometric'). Sample also includes the literal placeholder string '[ doesnotapply ]', a clear sentinel/junk value indicating the field is often marked not-applicable rather than truly missing - needs cleaning before use as a clean facet.

Name and samples ('2 taupe , 2 teal , 2 white') point to a color field, but cardinality is far too high for a clean color enum (4686 distinct over 26295 occurrences, uniqueness 0.1782 - much higher than tone_code's 9 or material_code_2's 77). Samples also contain junk/sentinel values - ';' and the literal string '[ tied to : color ]' (evidence of a broken export where a cross-reference placeholder leaked into the value instead of real color data) - so I treat this as color-intent but data-quality-compromised, better served initially by lexical fallback than a bitmap enum.

Despite the 'hue' naming, samples ('acacia','acorn','acrylic','aged brass') mix material names with finish/color names - this looks more like a finish attribute (material+color combined, e.g. hardware finish) than a pure color field. 1613 distinct / uniqueness 0.198 is high for a color enum, consistent with a finish vocabulary that blends material and tone.

Samples ('acrylic','aged ash','aged brass') overlap almost exactly with hue_code_2's samples, and both contain a junk numeric '0' sentinel - suggesting surface_code and hue_code_2 are parallel/related finish attributes (e.g. two different parts' finishes) rather than truly distinct concepts; 1294 distinct / uniqueness 0.1676 is consistent with a large finish vocabulary.

113 distinct values ranging from simple ('100 % cotton') to a complex multi-part composite spec ('10 % mdf/ 10 % half pu/ 10 % non-woven/ 10 % sponge/ 60 % metal frame') - an upholstery/fabric composition field. The composite entries are closer to structured free text than a clean single-select tag, so lexical search is a safer initial primitive than a strict bitmap enum.

Samples mix descriptive fabric-color names ('2 tone espresso','2-tone brown','2-tone latte') with what looks like a raw manufacturer color code ('0354-92 ; 0354-92') - a fabric-specific color field distinct from hue_code, but highest uniqueness of the color-family fields (0.2978 over 2176 distinct/7306 occurrences) shows it fragments into many near-unique swatch codes that shoppers would not type verbatim.

Only 7 distinct values with clean-looking short samples ('1 year','90 days','lifetime') suggest a bucketed warranty-term enum, but one distinct value is an entire run-on sentence with an embedded support URL ('...for customer support please go to https://blazinwheelssupport.com/') - a dirty free-text outlier mixed into an otherwise short enum, and the reported mean_value_length (2.77) doesn't reconcile with any of the 5 shown samples (all 6-119 chars), signaling this field's statistics carry real noise. I treat it as an enum-in-intent but not reliable enough yet for confident direct filtering.

12 distinct clean short values ('full','full warranty','limited','1 year limited warranty'), moderate occurrence (16579) - a normalized warranty-tier bucket, a plausible and common shopper filter ('full warranty' vs 'limited').

112 distinct values including full sentences ('1 year from the date of purchase.','1 year limited manufacturer warranty') vs coverage_tier's 12 clean bucket labels - this looks like the raw/unnormalized warranty text that coverage_tier was derived from, better treated as descriptive text than a direct filter facet.

Very low occurrence (546 of a much larger corpus) but extremely high uniqueness (0.9029) with descriptive multi-word samples ('1881 oahu hawaii vintage map','a pelican and other birds near a pool the floating feather 1680') read as artwork/print titles - a niche, category-specific alternate title field (e.g. for wall art), not a generic identifier despite the near-1 uniqueness ratio.

3500 distinct values with long mean length (50.76) and full-sentence care-instruction samples ('wipe clean with a damp cloth','clean or remove stains by using soap or detergent...') - clearly free-text care instructions, useful for keyword/contains search but not a clean filterable facet.

2706 distinct values listing package contents ('( 1 ) - kitchen cart','( 1 ) stand mixer , ( 1 ) 6 quart bowl , ( 1 ) wire , ( 1 ) flat beater ...') - a 'what's included' manifest. The unusual 0.1118 numeric_parseable_fraction likely comes from rows containing only a bare count/number. Shoppers do search for specific included components ('with ottoman', 'includes bowl'), so this has real contains-search retrieval value.

Near-total uniqueness (0.9785) with SKU/model-number-shaped samples ('06.mmfpbdv.44','069556530416' - the latter looks like a 12-digit UPC/EAN) supports a per-item identifier. However the sample '# ref !' strongly resembles a corrupted Excel '#REF!' formula-error artifact leaking into the export, a real data-quality defect that slightly undercuts confidence in this column's overall cleanliness. Shoppers do occasionally search exact model/SKU numbers for replacement parts.

descriptors.relationship_semantics: An identifier pointing to a different, related product (e.g. a companion/matching item, bundle component, or replacement part) rather than describing this product itself.
descriptors.evidence: Name ('linked') plus data shape support a cross-reference: only 78 distinct values across 161 occurrences (uniqueness 0.4845, i.e. many rows repeat the same referenced value, as expected when several products point at the same related item) rather than a per-row-unique own identifier. However some sample values are suspiciously tiny integers ('1','2') that look more like a position/quantity marker than a real product code, which tempers confidence that every value here is a genuine cross-reference.

descriptors.relationship_semantics: An identifier or paired identifiers referencing a specific companion/matching product or component (e.g. a matched set item or a paired left/right part) rather than this product's own code.
descriptors.evidence: Occurrence equals distinct count (71/71, uniqueness 1.0) with realistic manufacturer-part-number-shaped samples ('01-0619-884-01/01-0619-885-01','140-c6501s-t','1wf54a0jsv'). The slash-joined double code in the first sample ('.../...') suggests a paired reference (e.g. two linked SKUs), reinforcing a relationship/cross-reference role rather than a simple self-identifier - very rare occurrence (71 rows total) is consistent with this only applying to a narrow subset of products that have a defined companion item.
